note: Voss's own baking recipes, written for this package: one for each month, by the seasons where he was built, north of the equator. Vegetarian; eggs and dairy are welcome. Everything is weighed in grams, eggs included: they are weighed without their shells. The recipes were written with care, and nobody has yet baked them from this file: each stays marked untested until someone has, and says so.

recipes.name: Soda bread
recipes.why: January has no patience for yeast. This is bread in under an hour, for a cold house.
recipes.time: 40 to 45 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped underneath
method: Stir the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt together, then stir in the buttermilk until a soft dough forms. Do not knead it.
Shape it into a round on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake it at once, and cool it on a rack.

recipes.name: Pound cake
recipes.why: Equal weights of four things. A month with little to recommend it deserves a recipe with nowhere to hide.
recipes.tin: a loaf tin of about 1 litre, buttered and lined
recipes.time: 55 to 65 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean

ingredients.item: eggs, beaten, weighed without their shells

method: Beat the butter and sugar until they are pale and light.
Beat in the egg a little at a time, with a spoonful of the flour if it starts to separate.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, and scrape the batter into the tin.
Bake it. Leave it in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn it out onto a rack.

recipes.name: Lemon drizzle loaf
recipes.why: The first thing of the year that tastes of light. The drizzle goes on while the loaf is hot, or not at all.
recipes.tin: a loaf tin of about 1 litre, buttered and lined
recipes.time: 45 to 50 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean

ingredients.item: eggs, beaten, weighed without their shells

method: Beat the butter, caster sugar and zest until pale, then beat in the egg a little at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, loosen the batter with the milk, and scrape it into the tin.
Bake it. Stir the lemon juice into the granulated sugar while it bakes: the sugar should not dissolve.
Prick the hot loaf all over with a skewer, spoon the drizzle over it, and leave it in the tin until it is cold.

recipes.name: Plain scones
recipes.why: Quick, and unforgiving of a heavy hand. Plain flour and the baking powder weighed: the rise is his decision.
recipes.tin: a baking tray, floured, and a 5 cm round cutter
recipes.time: 12 to 15 minutes, until well risen and golden on top
method: Stir the flour, baking powder and salt together, and rub in the butter until it looks like fine crumbs. Stir in the sugar.
Pour in the milk and bring it together with a knife, in as few strokes as will do it. The dough should be soft and a little sticky.
Pat it out 3 cm thick on a floured board. Cut straight down with the cutter, without twisting, and set the scones on the tray.
Bake them at once, and cool them on a rack.

recipes.name: Sponge sandwich with jam
recipes.why: For a table in the garden. Two layers, one jar of jam, and no excuse for a dome: weigh the batter into the tins.
recipes.tin: two 20 cm sandwich tins, buttered and base-lined
recipes.time: 22 to 25 minutes, until the sponge springs back when pressed lightly

ingredients.item: eggs, beaten, weighed without their shells

method: Beat the butter and sugar until pale and light, then beat in the egg a little at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, and loosen the batter with the milk.
Divide the batter between the tins by weight and level it.
Bake them. Leave them in the tins for 5 minutes, turn them out onto a rack, and sandwich them with the jam when they are cold.

recipes.name: Flapjacks
recipes.why: Nobody wants the oven on for long in June. Twenty minutes, one pan, and they keep for a week in a tin.
recipes.tin: a 20 cm square tin, lined with baking paper
recipes.time: 20 to 25 minutes, until golden at the edges and still soft in the middle
method: Melt the butter, sugar and syrup together in a pan over a low heat, without letting it boil.
Stir in the oats and salt until every oat is coated, and press the mixture evenly into the tin.
Bake it. Mark it into squares while it is warm, and leave it in the tin until it is cold.

recipes.name: Oat biscuits
recipes.why: For a heatwave, baked at night: twelve minutes of oven, and the window open.
recipes.tin: two baking trays, lined with baking paper
recipes.time: 12 to 15 minutes, until golden at the edges and still soft in the middle

ingredients.item: egg, beaten, weighed without its shell

method: Beat the butter and sugar together, then beat in the egg.
Stir in the oats, flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt.
Roll the dough into balls, set them well apart on the trays, and flatten each a little.
Bake them. Leave them on the trays for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack.

recipes.name: Plum traybake
recipes.why: Plums come all at once and will not wait. The almonds are there to catch the juice.
recipes.tin: a 20 by 30 cm tin, lined with baking paper
recipes.time: 40 to 45 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the cake between the plums comes out clean

ingredients.item: eggs, beaten, weighed without their shells

method: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg a little at a time.
Fold in the flour, almonds, baking powder and salt, and spread the batter in the tin.
Set the plums on top, cut side up, and press them in a little.
Bake it, and cool it in the tin before cutting it into squares.

recipes.name: Overnight loaf
recipes.why: The evenings draw in, and the dough does the work while the house sleeps. It rewards patience, so he is working on it.
recipes.tin: a heavy pot of 3 to 4 litres with a lid that can go in the oven, and baking paper to lower the dough in on
recipes.oven: 230 C (210 C with a fan), with the pot inside from cold
recipes.time: 30 minutes with the lid on, then 12 to 15 minutes with it off, until deep brown
method: In the evening, stir everything together in a large bowl until no dry flour is left. Do not knead it. Cover the bowl and leave it at room temperature for 12 to 14 hours.
In the morning the dough will be bubbly and loose. Turn it out onto a floured board, fold it over itself three or four times, shape it into a ball, and set it seam down on baking paper.
Cover it and leave it for 1 hour. Heat the oven, with the pot and its lid inside, for the last 30 minutes of that.
Lower the dough into the hot pot on its paper, put the lid on, and bake it. Cool it on a rack for an hour before cutting it.

recipes.name: Apple cake
recipes.why: Autumn is his: cold dry air, the oven on, apples. This is the cake that goes with all three.
recipes.tin: a deep 20 cm round tin, buttered and lined
recipes.time: 50 to 60 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean

ingredients.item: eggs, beaten, weighed without their shells

method: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg a little at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then the apples. The batter will be stiff.
Scrape it into the tin and level it.
Bake it. Leave it in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn it out onto a rack.

recipes.name: Plain shortbread
recipes.why: Three ingredients and salt. November is for finding out whether the butter was good.
recipes.tin: a 20 cm square tin, lined with baking paper
recipes.time: 35 to 40 minutes, until pale gold at the edges
method: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt until it looks like damp sand, then press it together.
Press it evenly into the tin, prick it all over with a fork, and chill it for 20 minutes.
Bake it. Cut it into fingers while it is warm, and leave it in the tin until it is cold.

recipes.name: Gingerbread biscuits
recipes.why: December, and made strictly to recipe. The spice is weighed like everything else.
recipes.tin: two baking trays, lined with baking paper, and cutters of about 7 cm
recipes.time: 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges have just begun to darken

ingredients.item: egg, beaten, weighed without its shell

method: Stir the flour, spices, bicarbonate of soda and salt together, and rub in the butter until it looks like fine crumbs. Stir in the sugar.
Beat the syrup into the egg, pour it in, and bring it together into a smooth dough. Wrap it and chill it for 30 minutes.
Roll it out 5 mm thick on a floured board, cut out the biscuits, and set them a little apart on the trays.
Bake them. Leave them on the trays for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack. They harden as they cool.
